title: useradd-no-log-init
description: >-
  useradd with a high UID can add gigabytes to a Docker image via /var/log/faillog. Why useradd needs --no-log-init in Dockerfiles.
---

`RUN useradd -u 100000 appuser` can silently add **gigabytes** to an image. `useradd` initializes the `/var/log/faillog` and `/var/log/lastlog` accounting files, which are indexed by UID — creating a high-UID user makes them enormous sparse files, and Docker's layer format stores sparse files at their full apparent size. This rule flags a `useradd` that sets a UID of six or more digits without `--no-log-init` or its short form `-l`, the same cut-off as hadolint's DL3046. A `useradd` with no `-u`, a shorter UID, or a UID that comes from a variable is not reported. The rule reads only commands that run, so `echo "useradd -u 100000 app"` does not count.

## What the rule catches

```dockerfile title="Dockerfile — a high UID balloons the layer"
FROM debian:12-slim
RUN useradd -u 100000 appuser
USER appuser
```

Scanning this file reports:

```text
⚠ WARN [docker-doctor/useradd-no-log-init]
  RUN instruction runs 'useradd' with a large UID and without '--no-log-init'. A large UID makes useradd write a very large sparse lastlog file, and Go's sparse tar archive bug can then use excessive disk space.
```

## Why it matters

This is a genuine footgun (docker/docker#5419): the Dockerfile looks completely innocent, the build succeeds, and the image is mysteriously huge — nothing in the file hints that a login-accounting quirk from the 1990s is the cause. `--no-log-init` skips initializing those files, which containers never use anyway (nobody interactively logs into a container through the login subsystem). There is no downside; it's pure insurance.

## How to fix it

Pass `--no-log-init` or its short form `-l` to useradd when it sets a large UID (e.g., `RUN useradd --no-log-init -r -u 1000000 -g mygroup myuser`).

```dockerfile title="Dockerfile — accounting files never created"
FROM debian:12-slim
RUN useradd --no-log-init -u 100000 appuser
USER appuser
```

`-r` creates a system account (no home directory, UID from the system range), which is usually what a service container wants. On Alpine the equivalent tool is `adduser -S`, which doesn't have this problem. Creating a non-root user in the first place is the subject of [no-root-user](/docs/reference/rules/no-root-user).

The rule misses a few real cases on purpose. `lastlog` keeps a 292-byte record for each UID, so UID 65532 (the usual `nonroot` user) already makes a sparse file of about 19 MB, and a UID under 100000 is never reported. That size is small next to the gigabytes of a UID in the millions. A UID read from a variable is also skipped, because the rule cannot know its value. Add `-l` to those `useradd` calls if the extra layer size matters to you.

## Rule details

- **Rule key** — `docker-doctor/useradd-no-log-init`
- **Category** — Best Practices
- **Default severity** — `warning`
- **Applies to** — Dockerfiles

Explain this rule from the CLI:

```bash
npx @docker-doctor/cli@latest rules explain docker-doctor/useradd-no-log-init
```

Change its severity — or turn it off — in your [config file](/docs/reference/configuration):

```ts
// docker-doctor.config.ts
export default {
  rules: {
    "docker-doctor/useradd-no-log-init": "off",
  },
};
```

Severity affects the [health score](/docs/reference/scoring): `error` findings cost more points than `warning`, and `info` costs the least.
